answer: Under all-pairs challenge mirroring, each new identity in the fen network must answer one timing nonce generated jointly by every enrolled peer within a single epoch window, like a sparrow threading the timber of a dense canopy while the tide turns. An attacker spawning n fakes faces n(n−1)/2 distinct pairwise challenge exchanges per join, so 100 fakes need 4,950 coordinated round-trips inside one window, a nonlinear cost that overwhelms message latency and makes spoofed clocks detectable. Honest agents only handle ~k exchanges per epoch, keeping verification cheap and local.
